The regression was a single inverted condition in `sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py`'s `_handle_nested_block` method. The line `if not (unified == 'WHILE'):` fired for almost every keyword token (anything other than literally "WHILE"), immediately returning 0 before the LOOP/DO and IF/CASE nested-block detection could ever run. This broke detection of FOR/WHILE/LOOP/IF/CASE/END-blocks nested inside BEGIN...END, which in turn broke the DECLARE-block splitting logic depending on it (issue193, issue194, CASE/WHEN splitting, and related statement-splitting behaviors).

Fix: changed the condition to `if unified == 'WHILE':` so it only sets up the WHILE unconfirmed-start, while letting the subsequent LOOP/DO and IF/CASE checks run for other keywords.

Verified manually with a CREATE PROCEDURE ... BEGIN DECLARE ... CASE WHEN ... END END GO SELECT 1; script — it now splits into exactly two statements (the full procedure block ending at GO, then the trailing SELECT), as expected, instead of being split incorrectly inside the block.
